title: Visual Dependence Does Not Imply Answerability: A Systematic Analysis of Answerability Signals in Frozen InstructBLIP
abstract: arXiv:2610.17902v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Visual question answering models often produce plausible responses even when the available visual evidence is insufficient to support a valid answer. Although prior work has introduced benchmarks and abstention mechanisms for unanswerable visual questions, it remains unclear which signals derived from a frozen vision-language model reliably indicate answerability on unseen image-question pairs. We systematically evaluate answerability signals on a stratified 10K subset of UNK-VQA using frozen InstructBLIP, covering predictive uncertainty, cross-modal alignment, visual grounding, visual dependence, internal representations, and learned probes. Answerability discrimination remains weak, with test AUROC largely confined to 0.50-0.54. CLIP alignment yields the highest point estimate but does not significantly outperform generation confidence under paired bootstrap analysis. translated_title: 视觉依赖并不意味着可回答性：对冻结InstructBLIP中可回答性信号的系统性分析
translated_abstract: 视觉问答模型即使在现有视觉证据不足以支持有效答案的情况下，也常常产生看似合理的回应。尽管先前的工作已经为不可回答的视觉问题引入了基准和弃答机制，但来自冻结视觉语言模型的哪些信号能够在未见过的图像-问题对上可靠地指示可回答性，仍不清楚。我们使用冻结的InstructBLIP，在UNK-VQA的一个分层10K子集上系统评估了可回答性信号，涵盖预测不确定性、跨模态对齐、视觉定位、视觉依赖、内部表示以及学习型探针。结果显示可回答性判别能力依然薄弱，测试AUROC基本局限在0.50-0.54之间。CLIP对齐取得了最高的点估计，但在配对自助法分析下并未显著优于生成置信度。针对性移除与问题相关的视觉证据会导致（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文系统评估了冻结InstructBLIP派生的多种可回答性信号（包括不确定性、跨模态对齐、视觉定位和视觉依赖等），发现所有信号的判别能力都很弱（AUROC仅0.50-0.54），从而证明视觉依赖并不代表视觉问题真正可回答。
en_tdlr: A systematic analysis of answerability signals derived from frozen InstructBLIP shows that all signal families—including predictive uncertainty, cross-modal alignment, visual grounding, and visual dependence—achieve only weak answerability discrimination (test AUROC 0.50–0.54), demonstrating that visual dependence does not imply answerability.
